description: Figure 16b (“MMLU confidence vs. accuracy”) is a line plot showing how accuracy varies across bins of initial confidence for three series labeled “Final Accuracy,” “Δ Accuracy,” and “Initial Accuracy.” The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.05 to 1.00 with tick labels at regular 0.05 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, with major ticks at 0.2 increments. The “Final Accuracy” series is drawn as a solid blue line with plus markers and stays near the top of the chart, starting around 0.90 at confidence 0.05 and remaining roughly in the 0.93–0.98 range through 1.00, with small fluctuations. The “Δ Accuracy” series is an orange dashed line with plus markers that begins around 0.30 at 0.05, declines to around 0.10–0.15 by roughly 0.25–0.35, stays near about 0.05–0.12 across much of the mid-to-high confidence range, and ends near about 0.20 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” series is a green dashed line with plus markers that rises overall from about 0.65 at 0.05 to around 0.90–0.95 by roughly 0.70–0.95, then drops to about 0.80 at 1.00; all three series include vertical error bars at each confidence bin.
